# Getting involved in the community {.unnumbered}

The community is diverse and anyone can contribute without necessarily taking on an official leadership role.

## Core team

The Bioconductor core team supports the project’s day-to-day operation and development.
Its work includes maintaining project infrastructure, coordinating releases, and helping the community resolve technical and organizational issues.
Core team members bring experience from across the project, including software, infrastructure, and community support.

Members of the core team are listed on the [Bioconductor Core Team page](https://bioconductor.org/about/core-team/).

The core team is one way to take on a formal role, but it is far from a prerequisite for contributing.
Package authors and maintainers, educators, users who answer questions, and people who help organize community activities all make valuable contributions.
Many people participate in these ways without a formal appointment.

Reach out to the core team at <bioconductorcoreteam@gmail.com>.

## Community Advisory Board (CAB)

The Community Advisory Board supports the Bioconductor mission by coordinating training and outreach, and by helping users and developers participate productively and respectfully at every experience level.
The board also helps connect community members with events and opportunities to contribute.
CAB membership and governance are described on the [Bioconductor CAB page](https://bioconductor.org/about/community-advisory-board/), which also provides contact information and updates about membership.

## Technical Advisory Board (TAB)

The Technical Advisory Board develops strategies for the long-term technical suitability of Bioconductor’s core infrastructure.
This includes package addition and distribution, user and developer support, and tools for the broader developer community.
The TAB also identifies technical and scientific aspects of funding strategies that support Bioconductor’s long-term viability.
See the [Bioconductor TAB page](https://bioconductor.org/about/technical-advisory-board/) for its governance, current membership, meeting information, and contact channel.

## Code of Conduct committee (CoC)

The Bioconductor website maintains a [Code of Conduct](https://bioconductor.org/about/code-of-conduct/) page that redirects to the multilingual [Project-wide Code of Conduct statement for Bioconductor](https://bioconductor.github.io/bioc_coc_multilingual/) which is progressively being transfered to the [Code of Conduct](../code_of_conduct.md) section of this handbook.

## Working groups

The Bioconductor working groups - current, proposed, and retired - are described on [this website](https://workinggroups.bioconductor.org/).

## New package review

Every package submitted to Bioconductor goes through community peer review before acceptance.
Reviewers assess whether a package is suitable for Bioconductor and is usable, well documented, maintainable, and interoperable with the wider ecosystem.
The process is collaborative: reviewers provide actionable feedback and work with submitters to address issues.

Package authors can learn about submission requirements and the review process in the [Bioconductor package submission guide](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/).
Community members who actively maintain a Bioconductor package can volunteer to review submissions.
Reviews typically take 30 minutes to 1.5 hours, and assignments are distributed among active reviewers.
New reviewers are onboarded with at least one paired review.
See [Review Expectations](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/review-expectation.html) and [Volunteer to Review](https://contributions.bioconductor.org/volunteer-to-review.html) for details.
